steps.text: Place cauliflower florets into a large microwave-safe bowl with enough water to just cover the bottom of the bowl.
Cover the bowl loosely with waxed paper or a paper towel. Steam in the microwave on high until tender, 4 to 5 minutes; drain.
Place drained cauliflower into a food processor with goat cheese; purée until completely smooth. Season with black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Steamed Mashed Cauliflower
raw_recipe.description: Learn how to steam cauliflower without a steamer and use your microwave instead to make this delicious side that can completely replace mashed potatoes.
raw_recipe.name: Steamed Mashed Cauliflower

review.reviewBody: Having read the other reviews, I added a couple potatoes to the cauliflower. I boiled the potatoes separately and microwaved the Cauliflower. I put the cauliflower in the processor and mashed well, then loosely mashed the potatoes separately adding butter, garlic, & sour cream. Then I added the mashed cauliflower. It was actually delicious. My husband loves mashed potatoes and I don't think he would have known detected the difference if I hadn't told him. Without the potatoes, I thought the mashed cauliflower texture was a little off-putting. Since we don't really like the taste of cauliflower, I'm always looking for new ways to mask the taste because of the health benefits. I will make this again.

What an interesting variation on cauliflower. As others had suggested I steamed the cauliflower and cooked 2 small potatoes separately. Used the food processor for just the cauliflower after puréed added the potatoes and 1/2 of 8 oz light cream cheese. Then put in oven to completely heat up. Served with a roasted turkey breast, a simply gravy and a big salad. Will definitely make. I never met a potato I didn’t like but this recipe expanded the field.

I wouldn't say that this recipe gives something that tastes like mashed potatoes, but it make delicious cauliflower! I love goat cheese, and you can really taste it in this dish. I saute 3 cloves of garlic in 2 tsp of butter and added that and it was really good. Will make this again.

I steamed the Cauliflower and followed the recipe but added about 3/4 cup of cottage cheese with an herbal Goat ,cheese. I ,liked ,the texture ,most definitely like mashed potatoes. Although it really tasted great it did still have a cabbage like odor.

You don't need a head of fresh cauliflower. Frozen florets work fine. I don't use goat cheese, but fat-free (or low-fat) cream cheese instead. I also add a few herbs and minced onion when microwaving the cauliflower. We love it, but I wouldn't necessarily call it a true substitute for mashed potatoes.

I make this all the time! My husband even prefers it to the Carb Loaded potatoes. I add a teaspoon of Brown Gravy Powder, 1/2 tsp Onion Powder and 1/2 tsp Garlic Powder to it for that real potato flavor
This was pretty good although no matter what you put in it there is really no substitute for mashed potatoes! The only thing I changed was I added two capfuls of half and half and some salt.
Excellent and so simple to make,
This is SO SO good. I am probably the only person who does not like mashed potatoes. This is so much better. Thanks for a recipe that we will use often.
My husband loved this as a substitute for mashed potatoes. And, it's super easy to make.
I loved this one and plan to start making it much more regularly. It was my first time using goat cheese and it was delicious. Super quick and easy for a weeknight!

I made this dish and my kids loved it. I looked it up because I wanted to get my one and two year old to eat this head of cauliflower. It was so easy to make and both my kids enjoyed it. I do believe that if I had just given it to them like normal they wouldn't have eaten it.

The mashed cauliflower came out awesome. I added a little more cream cheese and a little more parmesan. Although it was freshly steamed and went right into the food processor it had cooled down some. I had to pop it into the microwave for about 30 seconds.

The mashed cauliflower came out awesome. I added a little more cream cheese and a little more parmesan. Although it was freshly steamed and went right into the food processor it had cooled down some. I had to pop it into the microwave for about 30 seconds.

Next time I'll use less cauliflower and cook it more? I did add some garlic, onion, and spice to help the flavor. Not sure exactly what was wrong. Everyone ate it, but made no requests for a remake like the roasted cauliflower I made.
Delicious and EASYYYYYYYYYYY!!!!! My husband was licking his plate!!
